blacklistabilityReview.evidence: Reviewed 2026-07-30. Fresh safe-tag reads at BSC block 113076787 via bsc-rpc.publicnode.com re-derived the 2026-07-15 findings: STUSD (0x806dd21af6de051fb811760a5768d04a99160eb9) wrapper() returned 0xb4d3c1bb59be7b419af4e10e9b240f425782b22a; hasRole(DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE, 0x9ab82f8e97bf3202173b92e06e6593f336b76ccf) returned true; wrapper owner() returned the same 0x9ab82f8e address and wrapper susdcToken() returned 0xad66385c6db496258771b5fd8ac376e3dd0d1536; eth_getCode on 0x9ab82f8e returned the 23-byte EIP-7702 delegation designator targeting 0x63c0c19a282a1b52b07dd5a65b58948a07dae32b. EIP-1967 implementation and admin slots read zero on both STUSD and its wrapper, so neither is proxy-upgradeable; the sUSDC deposit-asset proxy still resolves to implementation 0xe1bf9310f23db3fd05931aa89879d5247bb2a678 under admin 0x6158905db12bc51f01542048546f4ca14a7caa80 with paused() false. A safe-tag paused() call on STUSD reverted, matching the verified v2.0.1 source, which has no token-level pause or blacklist mapping: its _update consults the wrapper's getLockInfo(from) and rejects a transfer that consumes an unexpired locked amount, and the verified wrapper v3.0.1 restricts wrapWithLock(to, amount, unlockTime) to its owner or OPERATOR_ROLE and creates the holder lock before issuing. No arbitrary lock of an already-held balance or token-level blacklist function exists in the verified sources. This remains a direct, issuer-written, holder-selective transfer-lock surface, a possible freeze posture, not a confirmed direct blacklist. The verified sUSDC implementation retains pause, holder-lock, and burn controls (currently unpaused; the 2026-07-15 review confirmed a non-persistent owner pause() eth_call succeeds, showing live control). Issuer docs describe broader transfer restrictions than the deployed STUSD code, so verified explorer source governs deployed behavior. No separate official ToS, proof-of-reserves publication, audit report, or archive capture was located in reviewed public materials as of 2026-07-30 (the stoneyield.io 'Audited BSC contracts' claim names no auditor or report); that absence was not used as access evidence.
